sources.title: Project Gigabit network build contract - Kent
facts: The redesigned contract covers around 9,000 premises
The reported public investment is £26.1 million
The redesign followed commercial-rollout expansion and market changes
BDUK reports discussions about premises outside rollout plans
limitations: Contracted scope is not live service availability
Uncovered-premises discussions are not completed alternative delivery

sources.title: Project Gigabit network build contract - East and West Sussex
facts: The redesigned contract covers around 13,000 premises
The reported public investment is £25.2 million
The redesign followed commercial-rollout expansion and market changes
Public funding is focused on premises otherwise expected to miss out
limitations: Contract redesign is not completed deployment
Public-review or voucher plans do not prove orderability

sources.title: Project Gigabit network build contract - Cambridgeshire
facts: The redesigned contract covers around 35,000 premises
The reported investment is up to £77 million
The redesign followed commercial-rollout expansion and market changes
The page separates existing infrastructure, commercial plans and project scope
limitations: Contract scope is not current retail availability
Commercial plans and voucher projects remain planned states

sources.title: Project Gigabit network build contract - North Shropshire
sources.evidence_kind: regional contract descope and replacement guidance
facts: The original award covered 12,000 premises
The page records 8,500 premises descoped from the Freedom Fibre contract
In April 2026 BDUK added premises to Openreach call-off three
Call-off three also covers other parts of Shropshire
limitations: Historic build and descope figures are not current parcel service
Replacement-contract inclusion is not completed orderability

sources.title: Project Gigabit network build contract - Derbyshire Peak District
facts: FullFibre is no longer delivering the original contract
BDUK and FullFibre mutually agreed to terminate it
In April 2026 the area was added to Openreach call-off one
Call-off one also covers parts of Staffordshire
limitations: Contract termination does not establish local coverage
Replacement inclusion is not completed delivery or orderability
